topic: Tested Kimi K3 for Coding: Hands-On Developer Review 2026

key_points: Tested Kimi K3 on optimizing a Rust function using SWAR (SIMD Within a Register)
K3 took ~15 minutes and completed the optimization perfectly with no errors
Achieved 2% speedup on the program
Cost about $1 on OpenRouter for the task
Author concluded K3 could well be frontier-level as advertised
Kimi K3 is a 2.8T-parameter MoE model with Kimi Delta Attention and Attention Residuals
First open 3T-class model with 1M-token context window and native vision
Weights to be released by July 27, 2026
Kernel optimization: competitive with Fable 5, outperformed Opus 4.8 and GPT 5.6 Sol
Built MiniTriton compiler from scratch — beats Triton on certain workloads
Designed a chip autonomously in 48 hours using open-source EDA tools
Reproduced astrophysics research in ~2 hours (normally 1-2 weeks of work)
Ranked #4/186 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (score: 57)
Pricing: $3/M input tokens, $15/M output tokens — somewhat expensive vs average
Cache hit price: $0.30/M (-90%)
130M output tokens used in evaluation — very verbose (avg 63M)
Cost per task ($0.94) similar to GPT-5.6 Sol ($1.04), ~1/2 price of Opus 4.8 ($1.80)
Context window: 1M tokens (~1573 A4 pages)
Author ran K3 alongside Claude on normal coding work — couldn't tell them apart
Same tasks, same quality, near identical token counts
K3 API: $3/$15 per M tokens vs Claude top model $10/$50
Kimi paid plans start at $19/mo, $39 coding tier is far more generous than Claude
Claude couldn't sustain Fable access on $20 plan — quietly falls back to Opus
Author sees no reason to keep paying for Claude after testing K3
K3 is #1 on Arena.ai Frontend Code arena, surpassing even Claude Fable 5
Pelican benchmark: 95 input tokens, 16,658 output tokens (13,241 reasoning), cost $0.25
K3 accepts image input — multimodal capabilities
Token usage decreased 21% vs K2.6 on Intelligence Index
Notes that pelican benchmark doesn't test agentic tool calling — the real differentiator
